short: Thomas Cromwell was Henry VIII's chief minister, engineering the break with Rome and the Dissolution of the Monasteries.
full:
Thomas Cromwell rose from obscurity to become Henry VIII's most trusted and ruthless minister. Recognizing that the Pope would never annul Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon, Cromwell engineered a legal revolution, passing acts through Parliament that severed England from Rome and declared the king Supreme Head of the Church. He oversaw the sweeping bureaucratic modernization of the English state and the systematic dissolution of the monasteries.

His vast accumulation of power and reformist zeal earned him fierce enemies. After arranging Henry's disastrous marriage to Anne of Cleves, Cromwell's conservative opponents convinced the king that his chief minister was a traitor and a heretic. He was executed at the Tower of London in 1540, a decision Henry later deeply regretted, lamenting the loss of "the most faithful servant he ever had."
